title.narrative: Mexico Low carbon bus corridor project

description.narrative: 3. 3.,,The project development objective is to contribute to the transformation of the transport sector through improvements in the long-term sustainability, efficiency and quality of urban transport in Mexico City. The improvements sought (expansion of the bus corridor program, the maximization of modal shift, the use low carbon bus technologies) will result in major reductions in GHG emissions and local criteria pollutants. The project is intended to make use of several Bank financial mechanisms: a) the provision of a Bank loan will help supporting the financing of the corridor infrastructure; b) carbon finance, based on the application of the approved Transmilenio baseline methodology, will purchase certified emission reductions; c) with the help of CCIG funds, the introduction of cleaner bus technologies in the corridors will be facilitated by the creation of a fund to reduce the difference in capital costs between standard and low carbon buses. Project Description. Components and Activities a) Development of transport corridors. The current corridor proposal consists of nine corridors and the extension of the Insurgentes corridor. In the first year the project will support the implementation of two corridors: (i) Extension of the Insurgentes corridor with a length of 9.2 km and a daily demand of 50,000 passengers; and (ii) Eje 4 Sur with a length of 20 km and a capacity of 100,000 passengers daily. The corridors will include: (i) exclusive bus lanes; (ii) elevated bus stations for high platform vehicles; (iii) pedestrian facilities leading to the bus stations of the transport corridors; (iv) concessions of the services on the corridors to restructured companies using high capacity and low polluting vehicles; (v) promotion of clean bus technologies and scrapping programs for old vehicles on the corridors; (vi) prepaid ticketing service; (vii) centralized control and monitoring service; (viii) associated traffic management measures, including the interface with non motorized transport. The corridors will be developed in coordination with urban development, air quality, and climate strategies which together respond to the combined needs of economic and environmental performance and in accordance with the recently adopted climate change strategy. Financing of the corridor infrastructure is being sought through a Bank loan. Carbon finance will purchase the emission reductions. b) Introduction of low carbon bus technologies on the corridors. The field test supported under the GEF project has demonstrated the viability of low carbon bus technologies (hybrid diesel electric and CNG electric) under Mexico City field conditions. Very recent data further supports the assertion that hybrid bus technologies can deliver substantial reductions in GHG emissions, while lowering emission of local criteria pollutants. The project will support their introduction in the corridors by covering part of the incremental cost in comparison to the Baseline standard Diesel buses thus making it possible to initiate operation at a commercial scale and providing an experience of global value.
